audits.title: Audit of antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring for the management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
audits.standard: NICE guideline on antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia; local CAIR form
audits.setting: Older persons community mental health team, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board

cycle1.result: CAIR form present in 73% (new shorter version 37%); 63% of forms fully completed. 100% had assessment of causes, non-drug measures first, target symptoms and risk-benefit discussion; all reviewed within three months.

audits.intervention: Teaching session at team meeting, health board leaflet for patients and carers, and reversion to the original CAIR form.
audits.other_findings: Risk-benefit discussions were documented vaguely. Re-audit planned in 6 months.
audits.citation: Thomas C, Bhattacharyya S, Bond E. Audit of antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring for the management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S108-S109.

audits.title: Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia: An Audit of Prescribing Practices in the Harrogate Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults
audits.standard: NICE NG97 (June 2018) Dementia guideline and local trust guidance on antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring.
audits.setting: Harrogate Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 88% had assessment of sources of distress; 42% had non-pharmacological intervention before antipsychotic (58% after starting); 63% risk discussion documented; 63% baseline bloods; 54% baseline ECG; 33% of those treated over 12 weeks had discontinuation or dose-reduction trial; under 22% had physical health monitoring at one year.

audits.other_findings: Random sample of 24 from 55 patients. Recommended a pre-prescribing checklist and a system to flag when monitoring and review are due.
audits.citation: Wilson J, White N, Croft M, Ahmed S, Illsley L, Hughes P. Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia: An Audit of Prescribing Practices in the Harrogate Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S187-S188.

audits.title: Audit on Management of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms Among Dementia Patients in Humber Older People's Mental Health Services
audits.standard: NICE: non-pharmacological before pharmacological management; antipsychotics started low and slow; follow-up at least 6 weeks after starting
audits.setting: Humber Older People's Mental Health Services

cycle1.result: About 24% started on medication without trial of non-pharmacological methods; those started on medication were properly followed up; overall adherence around 75%.

audits.other_findings: Risperidone was the commonest medication (37%). Re-audit suggested in 12 to 24 months.
audits.citation: Adeoye S. Audit on Management of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms Among Dementia Patients in Humber Older People's Mental Health Services. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S211-S211. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.523.

audits.title: Quality of Antipsychotics Prescribing in Dementia Patients in Wakefield (WF9 Area)
audits.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics in dementia: initiation for severe agitation/distress under specialist supervision, monitoring and follow-up

cycle1.result: 24 of 63 with dementia on antipsychotics; blood monitoring 56% (13/24); ECG 50% (12/24); follow-up plan 81% (51/63); reduction plan 8% (2/24)

audits.other_findings: 8% (5/95) on antipsychotics without dementia diagnosis; an antipsychotic register was suggested.
audits.citation: Piparsania B, Marriott R, Sunder S. Quality of Antipsychotics Prescribing in Dementia Patients in Wakefield (WF9 Area). BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S159-S159. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10424.

audits.title: Prescribing and Monitoring of Antipsychotics for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia in a Community Older Adult Mental Health Service: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: Nottingham Area Prescribing Committee guidance EG019 and NICE NG97
audits.setting: Newark and Sherwood Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Target symptoms identified in 100%; delirium considered in 83%; risk of harm documented in 67%; risk-benefit discussion in 83%; review at or before six weeks in 80%; rationale for continuation in 60%; deprescribing considered in 60%; Trust Antipsychotics in Dementia Assessment and Monitoring Form completed in 0%.

audits.other_findings: 114 records were screened and only six met inclusion criteria. Education, better induction and system changes were recommended, with a re-audit planned including baseline physical health monitoring.
audits.citation: Hammed S, Wright R, Davis L, Tomlinson R, Sathian A. Prescribing and Monitoring of Antipsychotics for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia in a Community Older Adult Mental Health Service: A Retrospective Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S298-S299. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11707.

audits.title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Monitoring in Dementia Patients Prescribed Antipsychotics: A Multi-Centre Audit
audits.standard: NICE guidance and local trust policies on cardiovascular assessment, ECG, metabolic monitoring and risk–benefit documentation when prescribing antipsychotics
audits.setting: Three inpatient mental health wards across two hospitals

cycle1.result: BP, heart rate and weight recorded in 19/20; ECG on admission in 8; ECG before or within 72 hours of antipsychotic start in 3; QTc documented in 6; HbA1c checked in 11; ongoing metabolic monitoring in 7; no documented cardiovascular risk–benefit discussion in any case.

audits.other_findings: Medication was reviewed regularly at MDT meetings for all patients. Suggested actions include staff awareness, prescribing checklists and electronic prompts.
audits.citation: Song C, Finlay J. Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Monitoring in Dementia Patients Prescribed Antipsychotics: A Multi-Centre Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S285-S285. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11737.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit to Review the Use of Antipsychotic Medications in Patients With a Diagnosis of Dementia in Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults in West Essex
audits.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics for BPSD: documentation of BPSD, exclusion of causes, non-pharmacological interventions first, structured assessment (ABC chart), review every 6 weeks
audits.setting: Older Adult Community Mental Health Services covering care homes in West Essex (Epping, Uttlesford, Harlow)

cycle1.result: BPSD documentation 100%; investigations to exclude organic causes and delirium 91%; ABC chart 38.5%; initial 6-week review 59 (75.6%); subsequent 6-weekly reviews 43 (55.2%).

audits.other_findings: Documentation of environmental causes and non-pharmacological measures was too unclear to audit. A standardised antipsychotic review record was proposed.
audits.citation: Rao P, Chouliaras L. A Clinical Audit to Review the Use of Antipsychotic Medications in Patients With a Diagnosis of Dementia in Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults in West Essex. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S340-S340. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11831.

audits.title: Antipsychotic prescribing in dementia
audits.standard: Draft National Clinical Guidelines (Ireland) and NICE guidelines for prescribing in dementia
audits.setting: Psychiatry of Old Age service, Sligo, West of Ireland

cycle1.result: 58% (n = 29) prescribed an antipsychotic; non-pharmacological management, risk discussion and dose reduction or withdrawal documented in less than 45% of cases (range 33–45%).

audits.intervention: Changes to the proforma assessment tool to prompt these discussions.

cycle2.result: Documentation of these discussions improved (figures not reported); no impact on antipsychotic prescribing rates.

audits.other_findings: Antipsychotic use 50% in home care, 80% in nursing homes and 100% in hospital care (p = 0.077).
audits.citation: McLoughlin J, Roemmele E, Cryan M, Dolan C, McCarthy G. Antipsychotic prescribing in dementia. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S91-S92.

audits.title: Antipsychotics for BPSD: an audit of prescribing practice in a specialist psychiatric inpatient unit.
audits.standard: Standards derived from two UK dementia guidelines
audits.setting: Specialist tertiary psychiatric inpatient unit (St Andrew's Healthcare, Northampton)

cycle1.result: Of 60 patients with dementia, 50 (83%) had BPSD and 28 (56%) of these received antipsychotics; results generally satisfactory.

audits.other_findings: Room for improvement in documenting off-label use, screening for cerebrovascular risk factors, consulting relatives and using low starting doses with slow titration.
audits.citation: Haw C, Stubbs J, Yorston G. Antipsychotics for BPSD: an audit of prescribing practice in a specialist psychiatric inpatient unit. Int Psychogeriatr. 2008;20(4):790-799. doi:10.1017/s1041610208006819. PMID: 18307825.

audits.title: Antipsychotic prescribing in nursing homes: an audit report.
audits.standard: NICE-based: clear recorded indication or target symptom (100%); documented review by GP or psychiatrist in past six months (100%)
audits.setting: Dalmellington Medical Practice, Ayrshire; patients in nursing homes

cycle1.result: 22 of 81 (27%) nursing home patients on antipsychotics; clear indication in 11 (50%) and documented review in 14 (64%).

audits.intervention: Review checklist for antipsychotic prescribing in nursing homes and six-monthly review

cycle2.result: 15 patients (19% of 80) on antipsychotics; both criteria met in 100%.

audits.citation: Morrison A. Antipsychotic prescribing in nursing homes: an audit report. Qual Prim Care. 2009;17(5):359-362. PMID: 20003722.

audits.title: Audit of antipsychotic prescribing in dementia: Cambridgeshire results and lessons learnt.
audits.standard: NICE recommendations on antipsychotics for BPSD (severe symptoms, counselling, risk-benefit analysis, regular review)
audits.setting: Cambridgeshire mental health service (POMH-UK national audit)

cycle1.result: 9 (13.4%) prescribed antipsychotics for BPSD; risk-benefit analysis recorded in 6 and discussion with family or carers in 5; 3 of 4 on treatment over 3 months had two or more reviews.

audits.other_findings: In no case was the full range of causes or interventions explored; 10.4% were on three or more psychotropics.
audits.citation: Wightman R, Fielding J, Green S. Audit of antipsychotic prescribing in dementia: Cambridgeshire results and lessons learnt. Psychiatr Danub. 2011;23 Suppl 1:S126-9. PMID: 21894119.

audits.title: Antipsychotics in dementia: prevalence and quality of antipsychotic drug prescribing in UK mental health services.
audits.standard: POMH-UK practice standards for antipsychotic prescribing in dementia (including 6-monthly review)
audits.setting: 54 NHS mental health trusts in the POMH-UK quality improvement programme; older people's services

cycle1.result: 1620 (16%) without psychotic illness prescribed an antipsychotic; of 1001 (62%) treated >6 months, only three-quarters had a documented review in the previous 6 months.

audits.other_findings: Good practice in considering alternatives and documenting target symptoms; younger age, care home/inpatient setting, vascular or Parkinson's dementia and severity predicted prescribing.
audits.citation: Barnes TR, Banerjee S, Collins N, Treloar A, McIntyre SM, Paton C. Antipsychotics in dementia: prevalence and quality of antipsychotic drug prescribing in UK mental health services. Br J Psychiatry. 2012;201(3):221-226. doi:10.1192/bjp.bp.111.107631. PMID: 22790679.

audits.title: Effect of a multimethod quality improvement intervention on antipsychotic medication use among residents of long-term care.
audits.standard: Antipsychotic use only with a documented indication
audits.setting: 170 long-term care sites, Alberta Health Services (province-wide)
audits.intervention: Education plus audit and feedback delivered in a learning collaborative format
audits.other_findings: No increase in restraint use or aggressive behaviour; incremental cost $5 678.71 per inappropriate antipsychotic avoided; 75% implementation fidelity.
audits.citation: Hanson HM, Léveillé T, Cole M, Soril LJ, Clement F, Wagg A, et al.. Effect of a multimethod quality improvement intervention on antipsychotic medication use among residents of long-term care. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(2):e001211. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001211. PMID: 33846124.

audits.title: Psychotropic Medication Prescribing to Patients with Dementia Admitted to Acute Hospitals in Ireland.
audits.standard: Audit tool adapted from the England and Wales National Audit of Dementia (Royal College of Psychiatrists)
audits.setting: 30 acute hospitals in the Republic of Ireland, Irish National Audit of Dementia Care (INAD-2)

cycle1.result: 83% on psychotropics at admission; 40% given new or increased psychotropics; antipsychotics for NCSD in 11.8-17.6% and benzodiazepines in 4.5-7.7%; type of dementia specified in 52%

audits.other_findings: Poor documentation of risk/benefit and family discussion, and inadequate review for efficacy and tolerability. Baseline before a national clinical guideline.
audits.citation: Timmons S, Bracken-Scally M, Chakraborty S, Gallagher P, Hamilton V, Begley E, et al.. Psychotropic Medication Prescribing to Patients with Dementia Admitted to Acute Hospitals in Ireland. Drugs Aging. 2023;40(5):461-472. doi:10.1007/s40266-023-01020-w. PMID: 36995582.
